Definition: from G3565; a bride-groom (literally or figuratively):--bridegroom.
BiblicalUsage: Nymphios is the bridegroom. Jesus calls Himself the bridegroom in Matthew 9:15, Mark 2:19, and Luke 5:34: while He is with His friends they cannot fast, but the days will come when He is taken from them. John 2:9 shows the other side, the governor of the feast at Cana calling the bridegroom when the water has become wine.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Jesus chose the bridegroom's name for Himself on purpose, because a wedding is the one feast where joy is the point. That is why I hold that fasting has its season and feasting has its season, and while the Bridegroom is with us, joy is the right answer.
